t: According to the Book of Exodus, Moses was born to an enslaved people, raised in Pharaoh's household and sent by God to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
At Mount Sinai he received the Ten Commandments and delivered the laws and the covenant that Jews know as the Torah, which tradition has long held him to have written.

Most scholars regard the biblical Moses as a legendary figure while leaving open that Moses or a Moses-like figure lived in the 13th century BCE; no source outside the tradition points to him clearly.
dyk: In Jewish tradition Moses died at 120, with his eye undimmed and his vigour unabated, which is why the phrase "may you live to 120" has become a common blessing.
ev: Moses is born to Amram and Jochebed and hidden in the bulrushes of the Nile, by the Seder Olam Rabbah's reckoning
After killing an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, Moses flees to Midian and marries Zipporah
God appears to Moses as a burning bush and commands him to bring the Israelites out of bondage
After the Ten Plagues Moses leads the Israelites out of Egypt and across the Red Sea
Moses receives the Ten Commandments and the Israelites enter the covenant
The Israelites, afraid of Canaan's inhabitants, are condemned to wander for forty years
Moses delivers God's laws, passes his authority to Joshua and dies on Mount Nebo aged 120

f.born: In Egypt, to Amram of the tribe of Levi and Jochebed, according to the Book of Exodus; the Seder Olam Rabbah calculates 1391 BCE
f.died: On Mount Nebo, in sight of the Promised Land, at the age of 120, according to Deuteronomy; the Seder Olam Rabbah calculates 1271 BCE; his burial place is unknown to the Bible, and Islamic tradition places it near Jericho
f.role: Prophet, deliverer of Israel from Egypt and lawgiver, held by Jewish tradition to be the greatest of the prophets; most scholars see the biblical figure as legendary, with a Moses-like figure possible
f.known: leading the Exodus from Egypt; the Ten Plagues and the crossing of the Red Sea; receiving the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai; the covenant and the Tabernacle; forty years in the wilderness; traditional authorship of the Torah; a prophet in Judaism, Christianity, Islam and the Baháʼí Faith
